notes.title: Dust to the End on Strategy Fest Event
notes.content:
Hello everyone,

Steam Strategy Game Festival is now underway. To help more players become acquainted with "Dust to the End" , We will be offering a special 50% discount from August 29th to September 5th (Beijing time). We hope you enjoy the game!

https://store.steampowered.com/app/1074070/Dust_to_the_End/

[b]ABOUT THIS GAME[/b]

Nuclear war ended human civilization, but it could never uproot the evil within our hearts. Fight, trade, negotiate, raid– do whatever it takes to survive in the wasteland. You will have to be as clever as ruthless to thrive in a broken world, torn by war, cruelty, hunger and slavery.

notes.title: Dust to the End now with Full Japanese Support
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38107532/00a7d302790376517b2800ee1dd5c5db5e032884.jpg[/img]

Hello, survivors!

We know that surviving in a post-apocalyptic desert might be tough, so we wanted to make things easier… for some of you. Especially our Japanese players. Yes! Thanks to Azrael and the whole Japanese community, we can announce today that Dust to the End now features a Japanese localization. All you need to do to enjoy is keep the game updated on Steam. If you haven’t done it recently, remember that it is as easy as opening Steam and the game should update automatically (or just start the game and it should update, if you have automatic updates turned off).

We wanted to take this opportunity to send a massive thank you to our Japanese community! We know you are passionate about Dust to the End and you have done a hell of a job introducing the game to your family, friends and fellow gamers, helping to expand our community.

And now, let’s kick some ass on the post apocalyptic world of Dust to the End!

https://store.steampowered.com/app/1074070/Dust_to_the_End/

notes.title: Happy Halloween from the wastelands!
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38107532/7fcbb9619a0704e679958bce43daca4d4cc6b78d.jpg[/img]

Maybe you never realized it, but the idea of [b]surviving in the middle of a post-apocalyptic desert[/b] full of hostile creatures and selfish humans is... [b]quite terrifying[/b]. Monsters don’t just lurk in the dark, they also walk under the daylight -- and even your closest friend could hurt you in exchange for getting an extra portion of food. The sense of safety is just a delusion.

But hey, we didn’t mean to sound so intense! It’s just our way of setting the scene for one of the scariest events of the year -- yeah, we’re talking about [b]Halloween[/b]! And since we’re commemorating it with our amazing community after a weird, pandemic year-and-a-half, this time it feels even better!

In case you’re still not a dweller of the wastelands, you should check our Steam page to learn more about the discount we’re offering during the [b]Halloween Sale[/b]. Starting today, those users who buy Dust to the End will get a [b]25% off[/b] in their purchase. In other words, you’ll pay approximately 7,50€/8.99$ for the full version of the game.

If you follow [url=https://twitter.com/2Pcom]2P Games on Twitter[/url], you’ve probably seen that we’re also running a [b]flash contest[/b] to celebrate this spooky week -- and the celebratory art we designed for this occasion. It ends at [b]6 PM CEST[/b], so hurry up and share your answer with them! The best one wins a [b]Steam key for [i]Dust to the End[/i][/b], so if you’re already enjoying the game this is a great opportunity to invite a friend.

We’re eager to know about your adventures in the world of [i]Dust to the End[/i]! Remember to join the [url=https://discord.gg/xkPVydEfYU]2P Games’ Discord community[/url] to share your thoughts with other players, and let us know what you think about the game on the Steam forums. Also, here you can report any issue or bug you find so our team can fix it ASAP.

Happy Halloween!

notes.title: Q&A with the devs
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38107532/2ab4c854555f745e30f820dc023324b353965b36.png[/img]

Hello everyone! How was the weekend? We hope you were able to have some rest and a lot of fun. As some of you may have seen in last Thursday’s announcement here on Steam, Discord, and our social media profiles, we organized a [b]Q&A session with HaoJoy Game[/b] in our new [url=https://www.twitch.tv/2p_games][b]Twitch channel[/b][/url]. The event was hosted by Gurjiv Jaitla (@frozenbawz) and, apart from having Barry answering questions, we also had Steven Zeng from 2P Games participating in the conversation!

In this Q&A session, Barry and Steven told us all about the team behind Dust to the End, the origin of the project, its development process and the challenges they had to overcome, and finally the future of the project (and maybe other new projects?). We also talked about the gaming industry at large, and answered some questions that the viewers asked through the Twitch live chat.

As the event lasted around one hour, we’ve transcripted the whole interview down here! We hope you find all that Barry told us very interesting.


[b]GURJIV JAITLA (2P GAMES): How did you live the full release? Was it as good as expected?

BARRY (HAOJOY GAME):[/b] After the update from March to July, it’s generally OK. In particular, it has been understood and affirmed by many players.


[b]G: How many people have been working on it?

B:[/b] We are five people, including a producer, a game designer, two art designers, and a programmer.


[b]G: Is it the first game you make together?

B:[/b] Yes, it’s our first one. Only two of us knew each other before founding HaoJoy Game to do something cool, and we became good friends with the rest during the development.


[b]G: What is so attractive about developing adventures in post-apocalyptic settings? Do you devs enjoy destroying the world a little bit?

B:[/b] We wished that players could imagine the experience of starting from zero in a difficult situation like this. You know, it’s not easy to rebuild a whole civilization in such a hostile environment like the one you find in [i]Dust to the End[/i].


[b]G: Did other movies or games inspired you to create [I]Dust to the End[/i]?

B:[/b] Long story short, history itself inspires us. One day, we started talking about a famous man named Fidel Castro and the Cuban Missile Crisis. It made us think about a post-apocalyptic world and how our human beings could live in it. With a little help from other fiction works such as [i]Mad Max[/i] and the first [i]Fallout[/i] games, [i]Dust to the End[/i] was born.


[b]G: What makes Dust to the End unique compared to other strategy and management games set in a post-apocalyptic world future? Tell us something special about it!

B:[/b] In [i]Dust to the End[/i], players can build some industries in the city, and the supply and demand of these industries influence the output and prices of commodities. Players can arrange these industrial systems according to their own preferences. In essence, you run the economy by controlling the supply and demand.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38107532/7dcdb184617aab23799fe1c806c2550cbb2be505.jpg[/img]

[b]G: I’m sure that your workflow changed a lot when the pandemic got worse, and it forced everyone to stay at home. How did this event affect your way of working?

B:[/b] It took us about four months to adapt to this new routine and figure out how to get the most out of working from home, but after that everything was smooth.


[b]G: What are the biggest challenges/problems you faced during the development, and how did you overcome them?

B:[/b] The formulation of the art style. To be honest, we have changed at least two versions, yes, all overturned the re-established. We tried some styles and also spent more time in art design than we had first scheduled. After all, it’s a post-apocalyptic world and it was very important for us that the players could feel like they were living in that world.


[b]G: More and more developers are encouraging themselves to launch early versions of their games, so the community can help them to test advanced features or create a balanced combat system. How did this model help you? Would you use it in your future projects?

B:[/b] In the beginning, we just built the game we wanted. This program worked very well for us because it taught us the relevance of listening to what players expect from a game like [i]Dust to the End[/i]. It allowed us to solve many problems and try a few exciting suggestions proposed by our players, making the current version much more popular amongst our fanbase -- we gained their appreciation!


[b]G: How much has the game changed from your first idea until now?

B:[/b] Very much! In its earliest version, the game was very demanding. For example, you had to abandon your vehicle in the middle of the desert when you ran out of fuel. Of course, this is how it works in the real world but it’s a very inconvenient solution in a game where you just try to have fun.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38107532/f4a80c68713defa5b06fba5e907bd4d42401636d.png[/img]

[b]G: The trading system is a unique feature of the game -- it's way more complex than other turn-based sandbox strategy games with free-roaming like Battle Brothers, becoming pretty much the game’s core. Why did you decide to do that rather than focusing on combat?

B:[/b] Did you know that [i]Dust to the End[/i] was originally a trading game? The combat system is not such critical. The first lesson we want our players to learn is that, in this world, you need to earn everything by yourself. So you may eat worms or drink some expensive but dirty water to survive. When you get more money, spend more time, you could then work as a caravan having some adventure knowing the outside world, but also make some money by trading. As the key features for us are trading and going on adventures, the old version of [i]Dust to the End[/i] didn’t include the combat scenes you enjoy today; it worked like “Enemy show up!”, and then “you win!”, without any combat footage.


[b]G: Trade is very dynamic in the game, with prices constantly changing according to supply and demand. From a game design point of view, how does the game tackle this in a realistic (but manageable) way?

B:[/b] Industrial system. Every city has its own industry, and players can build new ones or upgrade existing ones. Every industry has output and demand.


[b]G: But this is not the only complex system we find in the game. Like it happens in any other society, players can establish friendly, neutral, or antagonistic relationships with other human groups. It must have been extremely complicated to perform since it has many consequences for the people living in the wastelands.

B:[/b] This is the choice we leave to players. Players will encounter many cities, gangs, and many events will be triggered. For example, if you have established a friendly relationship with civilians, you may not be able to get valuable rewards. But your team's mood will get better. Later, you will discover how important this is.


[b]G: Are these systems also affected by events where the player doesn’t take part? Like conflicts between human settlements…

B:[/b] If the player does not participate, then these events are meaningless, so we like it when players join them and feel them. So, not now. Maybe in the future, they will.


[b]G: On the other hand, combat has a simpler, more direct approach -- it reminds a bit of Darkest Dungeon, more so than more complex tactical, hex-based games. Why did you decide to do it that way?

B:[/b] We want the players to focus on growing their team in trading and social relationships so that they get more powerful in battle, but not overemphasizing the battle skills themselves. In most games, players can fight many enemies, just like that, without considering the context, character knowledge, and their teams. This is fun, but it's not true. We prefer to let players experience that you have no opportunity to fight against an AK with a simple knife.


[b]G: What comes now for [i]Dust to the End[/i]? As complex as it is, the game still has a lot of room for growth with new mechanics, locations, characters...

B:[/b] This is something we’d rather do in a brand new game. Maybe adding characters, cities, or events without further innovation could make players feel that the game is too repetitive.


[b] G: Is there any other project in development we should know about?

B:[/b] There is! It is entirely different from [i]Dust to the End[/i]. I can tell only two words today: simulation and real history.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38107532/a7f9250c04a225a2cbbe29943ea91c20dcf63631.png[/img]

[b]G: There’s been some controversy these past days regarding the Steam Refund Policy and short games. Their policy allows players to refund games if they’ve played them for less than 2 hours, but this is a problem for short games, as some players use this to play and finish the games for free. What’s your opinion on this topic?

B:[/b] At the beginning, I agreed with that requirement very much. I thought of it as a kind of protection for players until I played [i]FAR: Lone Sails[/i], which is a very short game I loved it so much! I think steam should also consider protecting these excellent games.


[b]G: What do you think could be a good solution for that? As you said, there needs to be a kind of “protection” for customers, but in this case, this is affecting a specific type of product, which are short indie games. What do you think could be done in order to cover both issues?

B:[/b] A good solution would be to use the Achievements system. There could be a condition that you cannot refund a game if you’ve gotten the achievement that indicates that you completed the game, so that this kind of dishonest player wouldn’t use this trick to complete indie short games for free.


[b]G: What other issues do you believe that need to be improved/addressed in the indie industry?  
 
B:[/b] I hope that many more players find their way to indie games in the future and learn to love them. And, of course, every industry has something that needs to be improved. But we are enjoying it, right?


Remember joining our[url=discord.gg/gR7E7rQGFN]Discord server[/url] to avoid missing our future meetings, ask other players for help and share your best moments in [I]Dust to the End[/i]. We're helping for you there!

notes.title: GET DUST TO THE END AT A DISCOUNT PRICE UNTIL AUGUST 23!
notes.content:
Good day, desert wanderers!

How is your adventure in the Wastelands going these days? A whole week has passed since Dust to the End was fully released and we still can’t believe the good results it’s having out there! According to Steam, our average of active players reached 416 users in the last seven days, and more than 750 people were enjoying the game simultaneously on August 15th.  Definitely, we must thank you for this: it wouldn’t have been possible without all of you who purchased Dust to the End and supported us on social media.

But this is just the prologue to a bigger adventure! There’s more to come in the following months and the whole team is eager to share this good news! Until then, we ask you to be patient and keep helping us in other ways: if you’re having fun in the world of Dust to the End, please consider sharing your experiences with more friends and acquaintances who love management games! Also, you can follow 2P Games on Twitter and retweet our posts from time to time. Have a question? Reach out to us on Twitter too!

If you still haven’t decided if you’d like Dust to the End or not, please read the amazing review made by Charles Ombler for Movies, Games, and Tech. It was a complete surprise to find out that he talks about the game as a kind of spiritual successor for the original titles of the Fallout series. Yes, the ones developed by Obsidian Entertainment! What else could we ask for?

Remember that Dust to the End is available at $8.99 until next Monday as a launch celebration offer, but it will cost $11.99 (excepting from sales periods) right after the promotion ends. Don’t miss this opportunity to discover one of the best indie gems of this year!

notes.title: Dust to the End is finally a complete game
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38107532/6a74f834aa3d5622554e5dd93ff5703fae5faa85.png[/img]

Good day, desert wanderers:

The full release of Dust to the End is finally here! As we shared with you all in our previous announcement, this new patch is bringing a lot of changes that will affect the gaming experience in a very positive way. We can’t wait to see what kind of businesses you will make in this arid land, and the consequences they will have for its dwellers.

We said this at least a couple of times, but it never hurts to remind you that our work doesn’t end here. Both HaoJoy and 2PGames will keep working on this project to make the best post-apocalyptic management game out of it. We’re currently working on vehicle modification and new plots, so stay tuned to learn more in the following months!

If you followed us for a long time but you still haven’t played Dust to the End, please consider supporting us on such a special day by purchasing the game! Just for a week, we’ll celebrate this special date by keeping its original price (7,39 EUR/8.99 USD). After seven days, the full release version of the game will cost 9.99 EUR/11.99 USD.

Finally, we intend to dedicate a “thank you” note to all the players who followed this project from the day it was published on Steam. This is something we couldn’t have done without your feedback and good will, so please feel proud of what we achieved together! We can’t feel more proud of our dear community.

No matter if you choose a dangerous path or start a new life far from trouble, try to enjoy your time in the Wastelands and make this story truly yours.

Have fun!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38107532/0199fcc1683119401ab51a156f3643c5dddeeb36.png[/img]

Below is our full list for our V1.00 Update:

[h3]New Features[/h3]
[list]
[*] [b]Language: [/b]Added Spanish version.
[*] [b]Maps:[/b] All maps have been reset, and mountains/blocks have been added. Players will need to explore to discover unknown towns and strongholds.
[*] [b]Tasks:[/b] A number of side tasks have been added, including new legendary weapons and new special accessories.
[*] [b]Endings:[/b] A highly difficult "perfect" ending has been added.
[*] [b]Exploration: [/b]Added map exploration events - discovering civilian camps, triggering additional events, etc.
[*] [b]Reputation:[/b] Added the ability to acquire civilian reputation, with permanent rewards.
[*] [b]Movement:[/b] Added the auto-pathfinding function.
[*] [b]Movement:[/b] Route correction function has been added. It can be used to move to your previous destination after pathfinding is interrupted or paused.
[*] [b]Music:[/b] Added a new BGM in the bar.
[/list]

[h3]UX Optimization[/h3]
[list]
[*] [b]Bases:[/b] It is now impossible to dismantle the base when it contains quest items in its warehouse.
[*] [b]Combat:[/b] The automatic combat function will now be usable in more encounters.
[*] [b]Log:[/b] Optimized the display of Quest-Industry and Quest-Property.
[*] [b]Crafts:[/b] Optimized the crafting items levels and formula.
[*] [b]Sound:[/b] Optimized some environmental sounds within the bar.
[/list]

[h3]Bug Fixed[/h3]
[list]
[*] [b]Traits:[/b] Baker’s unique traits has been modified: when supplies are used for the first time in each battle, your action will not be consumed.
[*] [b]Crafts:[/b] Modified the experience required.
[*] [b]Weight-bearing:[/b] The penalty for being overweight has been modified.
[*] [b]Combat:[/b] Team member mood BUFF and DEBUFF will now take effect in Autofight.
[*] [b]Other:[/b] Several bugs fixed.
[/list]

Your opinion and feedback are very important to us as it allows us to create a better experience for all players. So please, don’t hesitate to share your opinions regarding any of these changes, or new features you think should be added to the game. We’re eager to read them, so leave your message here or join [url=https://discord.gg/9xSkVjrXCf]2PGames community on Discord[/url].

Thanks for your time, have a nice day!

notes.title: Patch v1.00: A new adventure awaits you in the wastelands!
notes.content:
Good day, desert wanderers!

As we announced last week, [b]the full version of Dust to the End is finally coming this Wednesday to Steam[/b]. Today we bring you a [b]list of all the main changes[/b] that you will find on August 11th after updating or purchasing the game. Some of them are simple redesigns of the current features, but also you’ll find new functions as well as many new areas to visit in this post-apocalyptic wasteland you’re going to call “home”. We don’t want to bore you with too much talk, so let’s go straight to the point:

a) A complex world map with natural blocking elements where the path from one city to another becomes more difficult to walk. Journeys will demand more planning, and time to be completed. 

b) We will include new exploration areas, such as towns hidden in the wastelands, journey events and side quests.

c) Now there’s a “perfect ending” to unlock after meeting certain requirements -- and it won’t be easy!

d) You can obtain the Civilian status and get its rewards permanently.

e) After choosing your destination, you’ll be able to enable the auto mode so the system brings you there automatically through the shortest path possible. If a battle starts in the middle of the journey, the game will leave the decision of how to proceed at your choice.

f) There will be new Legendary weapons to unlock.


At the same time, [b]this update will optimize several existing features and fix issues[/b] identified by our team in the Early Access phase:
[list]
[*] Baker’s unique trait has been modified: your first supply consumption in combat won’t spend an action.
[*] Buff and Debuff status affect your team members in auto-combat mode.
[*] You can’t dismantle a base in which warehouse you stored quest items.
[*] The auto-combat mode will be available to use in more encounters.
[*] The display of Quest-Industry and Quest-Property has been modified.
[*] The crafting menu has been redesigned to make it more accessible and aesthetically pleasing. Also, the experience requirements to modify your equipment have changed.
[*] Some SFX have been replaced with high-quality music and effects.
[*] The number of medicines available in the black market will be significantly reduced to increase the difficulty of the game.
[*] The special effects of Legendary swords and machine guns will be increased.
[*] The Overweight penalty changed.
[*] You’ll find that a lot of things have changed in the dungeon zone, the “Bunker”. Environmental damage has been substantially increased and the monsters will be stronger than before. However, in exchange, the accessories you get in your raids will have much better attributes.
[/list]

Your opinion and feedback are very important to us as it allows us to create a better experience for all players. So please, don’t hesitate to share your opinions regarding any of these changes, or new features you think should be added to the game. We’re eager to read them, so leave your message here or join [url=https://discord.gg/9xSkVjrXCf]2PGames community on Discord[/url].

Thanks for your time, have a nice day!

notes.title: Dust to the End will be fully released in early August
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38107532/4c4dbcd0609e1c3870f5e0c68b7d7f0b57bb6679.png[/img]

Hello everyone:

This is a very special day for the whole team of Haojoy Game, since we can finally share with you that Dust to the End is going to be fully released in early August!

The idea of revealing the official date makes us feel excited, but we need to wait a bit more before that moment comes. Nevertheless, we can tell you the game will include two new language patches that players have been waiting for a long time: Spanish and French! This is happening thanks to our incredible community of players. Many of you have been working with us hand in hand to make Dust to the End a better game — and that’s something we’re going to appreciate forever!

Of course, these new translations will be open to corrections to make sure that everyone makes the most of their playing experience. Same goes for the current language packs in English, Chinese and Russian.

In addition to this, we’re glad to announce that our recent partnership with 2P Games, an indie publisher who you might know from games like Immortal Life, Nigate Tale and Zengeon; will allow us to offer a better community and support service. 

From now on, they will help us solve questions in the Steam forums and their Discord server is open for you all to make new friends, share your doubts about the game and send suggestions to improve it after the full release. We invite you to [url=https://discord.gg/9xSkVjrXCf]join them now[/url] and say “hi” in the main chat!

Don’t hesitate to leave a message in the comment section if you have any further questions, we’ll be looking forward to hearing from you. Thanks for your 
time and have a nice day!

Haojoy game
